chapter.v:
The wicked
flee when no one pursues,But the righteous are bold as a lion.

Because of
the transgression of a land, many are its princes;But by a man of understanding and knowledgeRight will be prolonged. [Ezek. 7:3, 5, 6; 11:13; Amos 8:2, 10; [Matt. 24:6,]

A poor
man who oppresses the poorIs like a driving rain which leaves no food. [[Rom. 2:6]]

Those who
forsake the law praise the wicked,But such as keep the law contend with them. [Ezek. 5:11] [Ezek. 12:20]

Evil men
do not understand justice,But those who seek the Lord understand all. [2 Kin. 21:12, 13; Nah. 1:9]

Better is
the poor who walks in his integrityThan one perverse in his ways, though he be rich.

Whoever keeps
the law is a discerning son,But a companion of gluttons shames his father. [Zeph. 1:14,] [Ezek. 7:10]

One who
increases his possessions by usury and extortionGathers it for him who will pity the poor. [Ezek. 20:8,]

One who
turns away his ear from hearing the law,Even his prayer is an abomination.

Whoever causes
the upright to go astray in an evil way,He himself will fall into his own pit;But the blameless will inherit good. [Ezek. 7:7]

The rich
man is wise in his own eyes,But the poor who has understanding searches him out. [Jer. 6:7 k Jer. 16:5, 6; Ezek.]

When the
righteous rejoice, there is great glory;But when the wicked arise, men hide themselves.

He who
covers his sins will not prosper,But whoever confesses and forsakes them will have mercy.

Happy is
the man who is always reverent,But he who hardens his heart will fall into calamity.

Like a
roaring lion and a charging bearIs a wicked ruler over poor people. [Deut. 32:25; Jer. 14:18; Lam. 1:20; Ezek. 5:12]

A ruler
who lacks understanding is a great oppressor,But he who hates covetousness will prolong his days. [Ezra 9:15; Is. 37:31; Ezek. 6:8;]

A man
burdened with bloodshed will flee into a pit;Let no one help him. [Is. 13:7; Jer. 6:24; Ezek. 21:7; Heb. 12:12]

Whoever walks
blamelessly will be saved,But he who is perverse in his ways will suddenly fall. [Is. 3:24; 15:2, 3; Jer. 48:37; Ezek. 27:31; Amos 8:10]

He who
tills his land will have plenty of bread,But he who follows frivolity will have poverty enough! [Prov. 11:4; Jer. 15:13; Zeph. 1:18]

A faithful
man will abound with blessings,But he who hastens to be rich will not go unpunished. [Jer. 7:30]

To show
partiality is not good,Because for a piece of bread a man will transgress. [2 Kin. 24:13; Jer. 20:5]

A man
with an evil eye hastens after riches,And does not consider that poverty will come upon him.

He who
rebukes a man will find more favor afterwardThan he who flatters with the tongue. [2 Kin. 21:16]

Whoever robs
his father or his mother,And says, “It is no transgression,”The same is companion to a destroyer. [Ezek. 21:31; 28:7 w 2 Chr. 7:20; Ezek. 24:21]

He who
is of a proud heart stirs up strife,But he who trusts in the Lord will be prospered.

He who
trusts in his own heart is a fool,But whoever walks wisely will be delivered. [Deut. 32:23; Is. 47:11; Jer. 4:20] [Ps. 74:9; Lam. 2:9; Ezek. 20:1, 3; Mic. 3:6 cloth and shaving their heads (see Is. 15:2, 3); (2) weakness; (Rom. 1:25).]

He who
gives to the poor will not lack,But he who hides his eyes will have many curses.

When the
wicked arise, men hide themselves;But when they perish, the righteous increase.
